column3: The Hebrew leaves David unnamed in both reign statements and says six were born “to him”; BSB supplies David twice.
The Hebrew does not repeat a separate birth clause for the four sons of Bathsheba.
The Hebrew continues the name list without a heading naming David’s other sons.
The Hebrew says sons rather than successors and repeats “his son” after Zedekiah.
The Hebrew calls these sons; BSB uses descendants.
The Hebrew uses singular “son” before Meshullam and Hananiah; BSB uses “children.”
The Hebrew says five without a separate word “others.”
The Hebrew uses singular “son” before Pelatiah and Jeshaiah and repeats plural “sons” before each of Rephaiah, Arnan, Obadiah, and Shecaniah.
The Hebrew separately lists the sons of Shecaniah and the sons of Shemaiah and places “six” at the end; BSB combines Shemaiah and his sons under six descendants.
The Hebrew has singular “son” before the three names; BSB uses plural “sons.”
